ink.note: Shipped as --color-ink-50…950 in src/app/globals.css (ramp listed 950 → 50). ink-900 is Ink Charcoal (#2E2A26); ink-950 is the dark-mode page ground.

surface.note: --surface: cards and inputs. White in light mode; ink-900 (oklch(28.8% 0.009 67.4)) in dark mode. Ramp lists dark, light.

kraft-soft.note: --kraft-soft: ground for a store's standing notes (pickup, delivery, notice). #F4EDE4 light, #3A3126 dark. Ramp lists dark, light.

accent.note: --accent: the store's colour as chosen (store.stores.accent_color), default Market Orange #EA580C. Not painted directly: the Tailwind `accent` colour maps to --accent-line, buttons to --accent-button. Ramp lists the defaults of accent-soft-dark, accent, accent-button, accent-soft-light.

accent-button.note: --accent-button, picked from --accent-button-light / --accent-button-dark. Light: the accent, or the nearest shade whose ink-or-white label reaches 4.5:1. Dark: the light button, or its nearest shade that is still readable at 4.5:1 and also reaches 3:1 against #2E2A26 and #1F1C19. Default #F5621F in both modes (ink letters at 4.51:1).

on-accent.note: --on-accent, picked from --on-accent-light / --on-accent-dark: Ink Charcoal (#2E2A26) or white, whichever contrasts more with the active button field. Default ink in both modes.

accent-soft.note: --accent-soft, picked from --accent-soft-light (default #FFE9DE; OKLCH L 0.955, C = min(C, 0.2) x 0.18, accent hue) and --accent-soft-dark (default #4F2515; L 0.32, C = min(C, 0.2) x 0.35). Notes, selected-state grounds, accent badges; always ink or mist letters.

accent-line.note: --accent-line, picked per colour scheme from --accent-line-light / --accent-line-dark on :root and .store-theme. Rules (.rule-dotted), borders, focus rings, progress bars, link underlines on hover. The accent, or the nearest same-hue shade reaching 3:1 (LINE_CONTRAST) on both Mist #F7F5EE and white (light), or on both #2E2A26 and #1F1C19 (dark). Tailwind `accent` utilities resolve here. Default orange passes in both modes.

muted.note: --muted (Tailwind text-muted): all secondary text. ink-600 in light mode (at least 5.5:1 on the page and cards), ink-400 in dark mode. Ramp lists dark, light.

script-name.purpose: Brand and sub-brand names only, set large; outlined to paths in the logo files.

stamped-caps.purpose: Second line of the name (FOOD HUB, BY YANG): uppercase, wide-tracked, between the sprigs.

caption-caps.purpose: Origin and category facts in small, wider-tracked uppercase, separated by middots.

store-name.purpose: The store's name in the store header only (or the store's uploaded logo instead); --font-yellowtail, Tailwind font-script. 2.75rem (sm: 3.75rem) on the menu page, 2.25rem elsewhere, leading 1.

stamp.purpose: Short facts via .stamp: Zilla Slab 600, uppercase, 0.08em tracking. Tagline, category chips and category headings (700), badges, the open/closed pill, order codes. --font-zilla-slab.

ui-text.purpose: The one UI text face: body, forms, buttons and prices. --font-geist-sans with Arial/Helvetica fallback; Geist Mono is loaded as --font-geist-mono.

accentTheme.logic: Invalid input falls back to #EA580C. Every derived colour uses nearestShade(): the accent itself if it passes, else the nearest lighter or darker OKLCH shade (lightness steps of 0.01, hue and chroma kept) that does. Letters on a button are Ink #2E2A26 or white, whichever contrasts more. accentLine: 3:1 against both light grounds. accentLineDark: 3:1 against both dark grounds. accentButton: label reaches 4.5:1. accentButtonDark: starts from accentButton; label reaches 4.5:1 and the fill reaches 3:1 against both dark grounds. accentSoft / accentSoftDark: fixed-lightness tints on the accent's hue.
accentTheme.activeVariables: globals.css sets --accent-line, --accent-button, --on-accent and --accent-soft from the -light values on :root and .store-theme, and from the -dark values under prefers-color-scheme: dark (re-declared on .store-theme because var() resolves where it is declared).
accentTheme.appliedOn: accentStyle() on the .store-theme wrapper (store pages) and streamed onto :root (admin). globals.css defaults are accentTheme("#EA580C").

narrative.overview:
The brand is the label a cook writes on a jar, a frozen pack or tonight's order: a connected brush-script name over stamped, wide-tracked slab capitals, finished with a drawn swash, two dill sprigs and a dotted rule. It is meant to read as made by hand in a real kitchen in Tapilon, and it lives where the kitchen's work already lives: the Facebook Page avatar, the site header and the sticker printed on every order bag.

The system is two voices and one saturated field. Every letter is charcoal ink (or mist on dark, or pure black on thermal paper). Brand orange is the one loud colour, used as a full field (icon, avatar, Android background) or as a fine dotted rule, never as letters. Kraft is the label ground; dill is only ever the sprigs; cabbage ruby belongs to the Sweet Treats by Yang band alone. Depth is flat print: no gradients, no shadows, no texture overlays.

The identity rejects the round food-stall badge with spoon, fork and ribbon. A round crop exists only because platforms mask the avatar that way; it carries no emblem furniture.
keyCharacteristics: Brush-script name (Yellowtail) over stamped slab caps (Zilla Slab), both outlined to paths in every logo file.
The d's exit stroke becomes a tapered swash that sweeps back under the whole of "Weekend" and runs clear of the capitals below.
Paired dill leaf sprigs flank the stamped caps.
Notched ticket corners (concave quarter-circle cuts) on the label and the square icon, with an inset rule that follows the notch.
Dotted rules and middot-separated rows of stamped facts.
Black-only versions that survive a 203 dpi thermal printer.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Orange appears as a whole ground or as a hairline dotted rule, never as type. Letters on orange are charcoal; kraft or mist on orange falls near 2:1 and is not used.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: In the marks, dill is sprigs and ruby is the Sweet Treats band. Neither becomes a text, border or background colour elsewhere. (On the website, ruby is Sweet Treats by Yang's store accent; see "Storefront theme".)

rules.name: The Black Means Black Rule
rules.body: One-colour versions are pure black, not charcoal, so thermal printers render them solid.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Script is for names; slab caps are for facts. No third face, no script facts, no slab names.

rules.name: The Feeling Not Schedule Rule
rules.body: "Weekend" is always set as a name in script, never paired with days or times in the mark.

rules.name: The Printed Matter Rule
rules.body: Every version must be reproducible by a single-pass printer. If an effect cannot be printed flat, it is not part of the mark.

rules.name: The One Field Rule, on screen
rules.body: The accent is a field (buttons, the cart bar, selected chips, progress bars, dotted rules) and never letters. Links are charcoal and underlined, with the accent only as the underline on hover. Admins pick the accent in Hours & settings, which shows a live preview and blocks nothing: the contrast rule adjusts the button shade instead.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule, on screen
rules.body: Yellowtail is only for the store's name in the store header (or the store's uploaded logo instead). Zilla Slab caps (`.stamp`) are for short facts: tagline, category chips and headings, badges, the open/closed pill, order codes. Body text, forms and prices use Geist, the one UI text face, for reading on phones.

rules.name: The Printed Matter Rule, on screen
rules.body: No shadows anywhere, including dialogs, menus and toasts: separation comes from borders and grounds.

dos: **Do** set every letter in Ink Charcoal on white, kraft or orange, in Mist on charcoal, and in pure black in one-colour versions.
**Do** use the compact lockup for headers, mono-compact for thermal labels under about 50 mm, and icon-small below 64 px.
**Do** keep the swash clear of the stamped caps; it sweeps under the script and stops short of the capitals.
**Do** give a sub-brand its own name in script and its own band colour on the kraft label, while keeping charcoal letters, dill sprigs and the notched ticket shared.
**Do** separate facts in a caption or category row with middots.
donts: **Don't** set letters in orange, or put kraft or mist letters on orange.
**Don't** use dill for anything but the sprigs, or ruby for anything but the Sweet Treats band.
**Don't** add a swash, notch or inset rule to the avatar or other platform-masked icons.
**Don't** build a round emblem badge with spoon, fork or ribbon; the round avatar is a platform crop, not a badge.
**Don't** add shadows, gradients or textures to any version of the mark.
**Don't** run the swash through FOOD HUB with a knockout; it was tested and cost legibility at the 44 px header size.
**Don't** lift the label's caption row into web pages as a small-caps eyebrow over sections; it belongs to the printed label.
